experiment.experiment.question: Does increased MLP capacity improve broad level completion under the same one-hour CPU allowance and the current ff12 training recipe?
experiment.game.name: 2aa2548-baron-timer
experiment.reference.name: ff12 (configs/hparam-1019_ff12_confirm.json): MLP 256x2 tanh, retained after paired-1019-v3

design.factors.held_fixed: every other ff12 setting: reward, observation, game, PPO, tanh, fresh init

experiment.seeds.allocation: matched: every arm trains once on each training seed; pairs are formed by training seed
experiment.evaluation.completion_definition: the game's level-complete event fired during the episode (evaluate.classify_outcome 'clear'); deaths or timeouts in the countdown after the last kill are not clears
experiment.evaluation.metric: completed clears per 990 episodes (99 levels x 10 episodes)
experiment.evaluation.aggregation: mean over training seeds and the bank's evaluation seeds; paired gain = arm minus reference for the same training seed, averaged over the bank's evaluation seeds
experiment.evaluation.checkpoint: endpoint model.pt (eval_every 0: no periodic test, no checkpoint selection)
experiment.search.procedure: fixed design: four predeclared arms, no adaptive search within the round
experiment.budget.hardware: local Apple M4 Pro CPU, one thread per job
experiment.stopping.rule: fixed 60-minute deadline-aware wall limit per job counted from launch (total_steps 1e9 never binds); no early or futility stopping; larger networks need not reach equal step counts
experiment.ranking.metric: mean development clears over the three training seeds and two development seeds (larger-network arms only)
ranking.tiebreak: mean levels cleared at least once on the development bank
experiment.selection.rule: the top-ranked larger-network arm is frozen, with its three endpoint checkpoint hashes and the reference's three, before the final bank is opened; no candidate switching or retuning on the final bank
